name: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (rooftop solar for households)
ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)
agency: National Programme Implementation Agency (REC Ltd); DISCOM/State Power Department as State Implementation Agency
period: Approved February 2024; implementation up to FY 2026-27 (outlay ₹75,021 crore)
whyItMatters: Sikkim is listed among Special Category States/UTs in the scheme guidelines and gets a roughly 10% higher central subsidy per kW than general states. Rooftop solar reduces household bills and diversifies Sikkim's near-total dependence on hydropower, which the 2023 Teesta-III GLOF disaster showed to be climate-vulnerable. The scheme also carries incentive components for DISCOMs and a Model Solar Village component (one village per district), directly implementable by the Sikkim Power Department as the state's distribution utility.
eligibleApplicants: Residential households (subsidy)
DISCOM / State Power Department (implementation agency incentives)
Panchayats/villages (Model Solar Village component)
sikkimNodalDept: Energy & Power Department, Government of Sikkim (state DISCOM function)
whatCanBeFunded: Central Financial Assistance for residential rooftop solar (up to 3 kW and group housing common facilities); DISCOM incentives for achieving rooftop solar capacity addition beyond baseline; Model Solar Village award of ₹1 crore for the winning village in each district; capacity building.
fundingAvailable: For Special Category States (incl. Sikkim): CFA ₹33,000 per kW for first 2 kW and ₹19,800 for the third kW — maximum ₹85,800 for 3 kW and above (benchmark cost ₹55,000/kW for first 2 kW, ₹49,500 thereafter). General-state CFA is ₹30,000/₹18,000 (max ₹78,000). DISCOM incentive rates: Not confirmed from available official guidance.
fundingRatio: CFA is a fixed per-kW capital subsidy (roughly 60%/40% of special-category benchmark cost for the first 2 kW / third kW); no state matching share required for the household CFA
nePreferenceDetail: Scheme guidelines set a higher benchmark and ~10% higher CFA for Special Category States/UTs — NE states including Sikkim, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, J&K, Ladakh, A&N and Lakshadweep (₹33,000/kW vs ₹30,000/kW; max ₹85,800 vs ₹78,000 for 3 kW).
stateContribution: None mandatory; state may add its own top-up subsidy
accessPathway: Energy & Power Department (as DISCOM) registers and operates as State Implementation Agency on the National Portal (pmsuryaghar.gov.in)
Empanel vendors, streamline technical feasibility approvals and net-metering under the state electricity regulatory framework

ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
agency: National CAMPA (National Authority) and Sikkim State CAMPA
subcategory: Compensatory afforestation and forest quality improvement

whyItMatters: This is Sikkim's own accumulated statutory money, not a competitive grant: levies paid by user agencies (including hydropower and road projects that divert forest land) sit in the state's CAMPA fund, with 90% of collections devolved to the State Fund and spent through annually approved APOs. With ~47% forest cover and continuous infrastructure/hydro-related diversion pressure on the Teesta, CAMPA is Sikkim's largest assured forestry funding line; Sikkim is already among the best utilisers nationally (97.7% utilisation; 609.52 ha compensatory afforestation raised, 92.3% of target, 2019-20 to 2023-24).
